canada.title: Montreal police arrest 2 ex-officers for alleged assault, criminal harassment, breach of trust
canada.summary: The two officers had previously been placed on administrative leave and then fired from the Montreal police service. They were arrested after Quebec's Crown prosecutor's office, the DPCP, issued a warrant.

canada.summary: A Republican senator says a U.S. defence department’s memo that reportedly placed restrictions on co-operation with Canada applies to things such as participating in think-tank conferences, not military operations.

canada.title: Premier Smith says amendments coming to Alberta's proposed bike lane legislation
canada.summary: Alberta Premier Danielle Smith told listeners on her call-in radio show on Saturday morning that her chief of staff met with Calgary Mayor Jeromy Farkas this week and that she thought the mayor had legitimate concerns.

canada.title: Nova Scotia community wins national history and heritage award
canada.summary: A small Acadian community organization has received Canada's highest honour in history and heritage.

canada.title: First residents to move into Saint John’s 70-home Sunnyside community in December
canada.summary: Three levels of government announced $17.2 million Friday for United Way Maritimes' Sunnyside community in Saint John, N.B. The 70 modular homes will house people experiencing chronic homelessness, with 24-hour support on site. The first residents are expected to move in mid-December.

canada.title: Pedestrian hit near Main Street intersection on Saturday morning
canada.summary: A single black running shoe was seen on the roadway along Main Street after Winnipeg police say a pedestrian was hit near St. John's Park on Saturday morning.

canada.title: Gander resident Matthew Collins faces charges related to alleged bomb making
canada.summary: Matthew Collins, who lives in Gander, is facing eight charges. They include possessing explosives and prohibited weapons, uttering threats and intimidation by using violence.

canada.title: Quebec to create plan to move away from fossil fuels
canada.summary: Quebec shared the news as part of its membership in the Beyond Oil and Gas Alliance, an international alliance of states and governments collaborating on phasing out fossil fuel production. United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres recently called on members of the alliance to each develop a road map for phasing out oil and gas.

canada.title: Edmonton community league, skateboarding group upset after city destroys ‘unauthorized additions’ at skatepark
canada.summary: The City of Edmonton has demolished part of a skatepark in the North Glenora neighbourhood, upsetting leaders from the community league and skateboarding community, who say the area was a unique gathering spot.

canada.title: Judge awards damages to both sides in lawsuit after neighbours' dispute over loose dogs 'spun out of control'
canada.summary: A judge has awarded an eastern Manitoba couple sued by their neighbour $10,000 in damages, and their neighbour $1,000, after an "unfortunate series of events" unfolded over dogs allowed to run loose on an unfenced property.

canada.title: From the ISS to the Yukon: Whitehorse students ask astronauts about space
canada.summary: Canadian astronauts Jenni Gibbons and Joshua Kutryk — who lived in Yukon as a kid — spoke to students from several schools this week. Gibbons was in Whitehorse, while Kutryk was aboard the International Space Station.

canada.title: N.B. publisher of Giller Prize-winning novel says win proves important stories can come out of the Maritimes
canada.summary: Susanne Alexander, the publisher at Goose Lane Editions, said Nicholas Herring was a dark horse in the running for the Giller Prize. When he won, she was ecstatic.

lines: Good afternoon. I’m Hannah Thibedeau, and this is your Palindrome News brief.
A behind-closed-doors meeting with the top officials of Stellantis about the sale of the Brampton Assembly plant was challenging but productive, Ontario Premier Doug Ford says.
A burst of violence in Mexico’s Sinaloa state after authorities captured cartel boss Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro,” left at least 11 people dead, authorities said Saturday.
The FBI is investigating an apparent hack of a national law enforcement database that it maintains, a person familiar with the matter said Saturday.
Trump orders federal contractors to check with White House before responding to Congress, The Canadian Press reports.
That’s your brief. We’ll keep watching, so you don’t have to.
